title: All Possible Full Binary Trees
statement:
A **full binary tree** is a binary tree in which every node has either `0` or `2` children. Given an integer `n`, generate every structurally different full binary tree that has exactly `n` nodes. Node values carry no information, so two trees are different exactly when their shapes differ.

Each tree is printed as a single line in **level-order** (breadth-first, left to right): every node is written as `0`, and a missing child of a node is written as `null`. Missing children of the last nodes are not printed, so there are no trailing `null` entries. (A leaf contributes two `null` entries only if some later node still follows it in the level order.)

To make the answer unique, print the trees in this **canonical order**: tree A comes before tree B if its left subtree has fewer nodes; if both left subtrees have the same size, compare the left subtrees recursively in the same order; if those are identical, compare the right subtrees recursively in the same order.

If no full binary tree with `n` nodes exists, only the count `0` is printed.

**Follow-up:** Discuss the recursion behind your solution. Why can a full binary tree only have an odd number of nodes, how does the number of trees grow (Catalan numbers), what do memoization and sharing identical subtrees save, and what is the time and space complexity in terms of the output size?
outputFormat: First line: the number of trees `T`. Then `T` lines, one per tree in canonical order, each a space-separated level-order serialization using `0` and `null`. If `T = 0`, only that first line is printed.
constraints: The depth of every generated tree is at most 9, so recursive solutions are safe.

examples.explanation: Two shapes exist. In the first, the left subtree is a single node and the right subtree has 3 nodes (root, then a leaf on the left and a node with two leaves on the right). In the second the sizes are swapped. The tree with the smaller left subtree is printed first.

examples.explanation: Left subtrees of sizes 1, 3 and 5 give 1, 1 and 2 left shapes respectively, combined with right subtrees of sizes 5, 3 and 1 (2, 1 and 1 shapes). That is 2 + 1 + 2 = 5 trees, listed by increasing left size and, within the same left size, by the order of the sub-shapes.
Every node has 0 or 2 children, so the node count of a full binary tree is always odd. No tree has 4 nodes.

complexity.time: O(T · n), where T is the number of trees (a Catalan number)

hints: Think about the root: the remaining n - 1 nodes are split between the left and right subtrees. Which sizes are possible for each side?
Let trees(s) be the list of all full binary trees with s nodes. Combine every tree of trees(a) with every tree of trees(s - 1 - a) for odd a.
Memoize trees(s) by size, and reuse (share) the same subtree objects when building bigger trees, so work is not repeated. Serialize each tree only at the end.
